newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's says Japan financial firms face challenges.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says Japan financial firms face challenges.

text.p: Japan's "Big Four" securities houses are facing a dual challenge of deregulation at home and growing competition in the rapidly expanding global market, Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday.
The Big Four are Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd, Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.

While the four firms are well supported by adequate capitalisation and a good domestic network, they face tough challenges to become prominent global players, Moody's said in its annual report on the industry.
A Moody's spokeswoman said that the report did not take into account the Nomura scandal that broke last week.
Nomura announced that two of its directors improperly moved funds into an account held by a corporate customer that media reports have linked to a former racketeer.
Moody's said that deregulation in Japan's financial markets would not pose a major threat to the large domestic business of Nomura and Daiwa.
However, Nikko is being currently reviewed for possible downgrading in the light of the impact of deregulation on Nikko's "predominantly domestic franchise", it said.
Yamaichi is less robust and more vulnerable than its rivals, but Moody's predicted it would receive government support if in trouble.

To compensate for shrinking domestic revenues following liberalisation of the current fixed commission system and the elimination of barriers separating banks and securities firms, the Big Four must introduce new products and services at home, it said.

"Simultaneously, the firms' management will find it necessary to strengthen their overseas capabilities to successfully capture market share of global capital flows against fierce competition," it said.
The number of second-tier brokerages is likely to decline significantly through consolidations, failures in the process of deregulation and tie-ups with foreign brokers, it said.
